notes:
CIRCUIT: a single rectangular frame with three horizontal rungs between two vertical rails. Left rail x~377 runs y~372 to y~565; right rail x~724 runs y~360 to y~558. Top rung (y~373) carries the 200uF capacitor (#0) at x~454. Middle rung (y~445-455) carries the 1kOhm resistor (#2) at x~491 and, in series with it, the coil (#1, labelled '50 mF') at x~640. Bottom rung (y~558-561) carries the 5A DC current source (#3) at x~539, arrow pointing left. A GND symbol (#4) hangs from the bottom rung at x~690 via a short vertical stem.

NET MAP (3 nets, 5 components):
  n1 = the LEFT rail (x~377, y 372-565) together with the three rung stubs that run to it: the top rung from x~377 to the capacitor's left plate, the middle rung from x~377 to the resistor's left lead, and the bottom rung from x~377 to the current source's left terminal. Terminals: 0.0 (left plate of the 200uF cap), 2.0 (left end of the 1k), 3.0 (left terminal of the 5A source).
  n2 = the short wire between the right end of the 1kOhm resistor (553,451) and the left end of the coil (579,449) - an inkmap dump at (566,450) shows this is one solid unbroken stroke ~27 px long. Terminals: 2.1, 1.0.
  0  = the RIGHT rail (x~724) together with the top rung from the capacitor's right plate to x~724, the middle rung from the coil's right end to x~724, the bottom rung from the current source's right terminal to x~724, and the GND stem at x~690. Terminals: 0.1, 1.1, 3.1, 4.0 (GND).

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITE DECISIONS (all three CRITICAL sites inspected in the crops):
  S3 (724,440) -> JUNCTION. Clean T, deg=3: the right rail runs vertically through and the middle rung terminates on it from the left; the rung does not continue past the rail. The reported dot ratio 2.5 is just the extra ink of the T corner, and the reading does not depend on it - a T has no crossing interpretation. If this were NOT joined, the coil's right lead would sit on a one-terminal net and the whole resistor+coil rung would be a dead branch with no return, which contradicts the drawing.
  S4 (376,455) -> JUNCTION. Clean T, deg=3: the left rail runs vertically through and the middle rung leaves it to the right. Not joining would strand the resistor's left lead alone and break the resistor/coil rung's other end.
  S11 (691,558) -> JUNCTION. deg=4. Here the bottom rung arriving from the left, the short GND stem dropping down at x~690, and the bottom end of the right rail (which turns the corner at x~724) all meet. The crop shows a plain T for the GND stem on a continuous horizontal rail, with the rail then running on to the corner - no hop, no jog, nothing passing over anything. This is what puts the right-hand net on '0'. The crossing reading would separate the GND stem from the rail, leaving GND on a one-terminal net and the circuit with no ground reference; it would also have to break either the current source's return or the right rail. Rule 1 settles it: junction.
  There are no solder dots and no hops/jogs anywhere on this sheet; every wire-to-wire meeting is a T or a rectangle corner, so no plain-X tie-breaking was needed.

NON-CRITICAL SITES (left at tracer default, none change the netlist): S1 is the '200uF' label ink over the top rung; S5, S6, S7 and S8 are the '50 mF' and '1kOhm' label glyphs touching the coil, the resistor and the middle rung; S13, S14 and S15 are the '5A' label ink touching the current-source outline. All are text-to-ink contacts, not wire-to-wire.

PORTS: no overrides. All four 'unused port candidate' warnings are label glyphs brushing a symbol box - (486,338) is the tail of the 'F' in '200uF', (628,471) and (492,479) are the tops of the '50 mF' and '1kOhm' glyphs, (518,604) is the '5' of '5A'. The ->t0/->t1 ports are the genuine leads in every case. All components are 2-terminal (or 1-terminal GND) so terminal order is unscored; for the record #3's t0 is the left terminal (481,561) and t1 the right (596,561), with the source arrow pointing left, i.e. conventional current flows from the right rail toward the left rail inside the source.

CLASSES: no overrides, but one label/symbol mismatch worth flagging for the record. Component #1 is annotated 'Inductor' by COCO and is unmistakably DRAWN as an inductor (three loops of a coil, identical in style to other inductors in this dataset), yet the drafter has written '50 mF' beside it - a capacitance unit. The GT must describe the drawn symbol, and the drawn symbol is a coil, so Inductor stands; the '50 mF' is almost certainly the drafter writing the wrong unit for 50 mH. I am NOT proposing a class change, only noting the inconsistency. Everything else (200uF two-plate capacitor, 1kOhm zig-zag resistor, circled arrow DC current source, ground rake) matches its label and class. Nothing left unresolved.
